description: F2P/P2P classification of this task's graded observations. F2P fail on the delivered state and pass after the reference repair; P2P pass on both. Measured in the task image, not derived from names. tests/grade.py reads this file and runs exactly the observations it names.

groups.requirement: Scheduler.enqueue_request returns true for accepted requests and false for duplicates. dont_filter bypasses duplicate filtering (without recording the bypassed request as seen). Default RFPDupeFilter identity uses canonical URL, method and body, ignoring headers and fragments; verbatim_url preserves URL spelling including fragments. BaseDupeFilter does not reject duplicates. With no JOBDIR, requests use memory queues. Higher request priority is served first throughout draining; equal-priority ordinary requests use LIFO by default or FIFO when configured. Start requests use a separate FIFO lane by default, after ordinary requests of equal priority; SCHEDULER_START_MEMORY_QUEUE=None disables this separation. Accepted requests increment total and memory enqueue statistics; returned requests increment corresponding dequeue statistics, while empty reads return None without incrementing them. len reports pending requests and has_pending_requests reports whether any remain. The normal open/close lifecycle initializes and releases the scheduler.

Request arguments, defaults and attributes behave as request-response.rst documents.
Request.copy() and replace() copy members and shallow-copy meta and cb_kwargs as documented.
Request.to_dict/request_from_dict, from_curl/to_curl and NO_CALLBACK behave as documented.
fingerprint() and RequestFingerprinter: bytes, method/body/include_headers, verbatim_url and REQUEST_FINGERPRINTER_CLASS.
FormRequest formdata and JsonRequest data/dumps_kwargs/headers behave as documented.
Response arguments, attributes, copy/replace, urljoin, follow and follow_all behave as documented.
TextResponse/HtmlResponse/XmlResponse encoding, text, selectors, json(), urljoin and follow behave as documented.
Headers is a case-insensitive multi-value dictionary as documented.
With JOBDIR the scheduler persists requests and seen fingerprints and resumes them; unserializable requests stay in memory.
Scheduler queues (memory/disk, FIFO/LIFO) and ScrapyPriorityQueue order, persist and resume requests as documented.
RFPDupeFilter and BaseDupeFilter filter duplicates as documented, including requests.seen persistence.
The SpiderState extension saves and loads spider.state in the job directory.
AutoThrottle enables, starts and adjusts download delays as autothrottle.rst documents.
Scrapy exceptions carry their documented attributes and are raised where documented.
scrapy.utils.url helpers behave as their docstrings state.
scrapy.utils.response and scrapy.utils.request helpers behave as their docstrings state.
DepthMiddleware tracks depth, enforces DEPTH_LIMIT, adjusts priority by DEPTH_PRIORITY and honours depth_reset.
HttpErrorMiddleware filters non-2xx responses unless allowed by settings, spider attribute or request meta.
RefererMiddleware populates Referer according to REFERRER_POLICY, meta, the response header and the policy classes.
UrlLength, Start, MetaCopyDetection and BaseSpiderMiddleware behave as documented.
CookiesMiddleware sends and stores cookies, supports cookiejar sessions, dont_merge_cookies and COOKIES_ENABLED as documented.
DefaultHeaders, DownloadTimeout, UserAgent and DownloaderStats middlewares behave as documented.
HttpAuthMiddleware adds Basic auth from settings or request meta only for the configured domain.
HttpCacheMiddleware, its policies and the filesystem storage cache responses as documented.
HttpCompressionMiddleware decodes gzip/deflate/br responses and honours COMPRESSION_ENABLED.
HttpProxyMiddleware sets proxies from request meta and environment variables as documented.
OffsiteMiddleware filters requests outside allowed_domains, honours allow_offsite and should_follow.
RedirectMiddleware follows redirects, records redirect_urls/reasons, honours REDIRECT_MAX_TIMES and opt-outs.
MetaRefreshMiddleware follows meta refresh as documented, honouring its settings and dont_redirect.
RetryMiddleware and get_retry_request retry as documented (codes, exceptions, limits, priority, opt-outs).
RobotsTxtMiddleware obeys robots.txt with the documented user agent selection and parsers.
